Q: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement concerns the parking lot collision
you reported in Houston, Texas. Please sttae your full name for the record.
A: Sorry, I'm not comfortable giving my full name on a recording just yet. You can refer to me as the driver of the silver
sedan.
Q: That's fine for now. Can you describe what happened when you were leaving the parking spot?
A: I had just backed out slowly, checking my mirrors like always. A pickup came down the aisle fasetr than I expected
and clipped the rear quarter panel of my car. I braked hard, and the jolt threw me against the steering wheel and then
the door frame.
Q: Did you have any part of your body injured in the collision?
A: Yes. I put my left arm out to brace myself, and my wrist hit the console. The doctor at the urgent care clinic said it's
a fracture. They put me in a splint and told me I'll need to see a specialist.
Q: Do you know which way the pickup was traveling, and was it moving before you started to back out?
A: It was coming from the far end of the row, moving toward the exit. I didn't see it until it was already close. I can't
say for certain how fast it was going.
Q: Did anyone witness the collision, or did you take any photographs of the scene?
A: A man in the next row got out of his car to look, but I didn't get his contact details. I took a few photos of both
vehicles before I left the lot.
Q: Have you received any medical treatment beyond the urgent care visit?
A: Not yet. I have a follow-up appointment scheduled with an orthopedic specialist, and I'm waiting on the imaging
results.
Q: Thank you. Is there anything you would like to add to your statement?
A: Only that I want my car repaired properly and my medical bills taken care of. I've been without my usual
transportation for a while now, and it's been stressful.
Q: Understood. This concludes the recorded statement. Thank you.
A: Thank you.
</page>

injury. Do not list the date of a note, letter, report, visit, statement, filing or signature.

it is the loss date. Examples: "Date of loss:", "Crash date:", "Date of injury:", "the collision on".
